post.caption:
ATMs were supposed to end bank tellers, and teller numbers rose for decades because cheaper branches meant more branches and the job shifted to selling and advising. Spreadsheets did the same to bookkeeping. The pattern is that tasks get automated before whole jobs do. The honest differences this time are the speed of adoption and the fact that cognitive work is affected, not just manual. Aggregate numbers can look fine while the disruption is total for whoever it lands on.
